items.stem: Under IFRS 15, revenue is recognised when:

options.text: The entity satisfies a performance obligation by transferring control of a good or service
options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 15 recognises revenue on transfer of control for each performance obligation.

options.text: Cash is received from the customer
options.rationale: IFRS 15 is not a cash-based model.
Signing a contract does not by itself trigger revenue.
Production alone does not transfer control.

items.explanation: Correct: IFRS 15 recognises revenue on transfer of control for each performance obligation.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An entity controls another entity for consolidation purposes when it has:

options.text: Power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to affect those returns
options.rationale: Correct: IFRS 10 defines control using these three elements.

options.text: More than 20% of the voting rights only
options.rationale: 20% ordinarily indicates significant influence, not control.

options.text: A seat on the board only
options.rationale: A board seat alone does not establish control.
A supply contract does not by itself confer control.

items.explanation: Correct: IFRS 10 defines control using these three elements.
